claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder has standard morphology and composition suitable for LPBF.
The intervention uses approximately 30% lower laser power density than conventional processing.
The intervention uses a scanning speed approximately 20% faster than conventional processing.
The intervention preheats the build substrate to 200–300°C.
The modified laser parameters and substrate preheating lower peak thermal gradients during deposition.
The proposed processing window applies to miniature components with feature sizes of 1–5 mm.
The modified thermal input produces relatively gradual solidification and develops nonequilibrium chemical short-range order.
Lower instantaneous thermal load reduces steep thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients moderate the cooling rate.
The moderated cooling rate facilitates formation and retention of a beneficial nonequilibrium SRO state.
Nonequilibrium SRO dissipates residual stresses.
Nonequilibrium SRO improves microstructural integrity and mechanical properties.
The modified process will significantly reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
The modified process will produce higher tensile strength and ductility than conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
The modified process will reduce the need for extensive post-build stress-relief treatments.
Conventional high-power LPBF without substrate preheating typically produces steep thermal gradients, high residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties in AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing laser power may impair full densification and thereby limit the benefits of the intervention.
Substrate preheating below 200°C may be insufficient.
Effectiveness on geometries larger than the specified miniature scale is unverified.
The contribution of nonequilibrium SRO to the predicted improvements in AlCrFeNiSi requires experimental validation.
